instructions: Put 1 1/2 cups water and the cinnamon stick in a medium saucepan, cover it and bring it to a boil over high heat. Turn the heat down to low and simmer for 5 minutes, until the water turns pale brown and smells of cinnamon.
Meanwhile, put the 1/3 cup oats and 2 cups of the milk in a blender and blend for about 1 minute, until smooth.
Pour the oat milk into the saucepan, then add the remaining 2/3 cup milk and the 1/3 cup sugar. Stir well.

Turn the heat to medium and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until it's thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Keep stirring the whole time, or it'll catch and scorch on the bottom.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the 1 tsp vanilla. Taste it, and add a little more sugar if you'd like it sweeter.
Fish out the cinnamon stick. Pour the atole into 4 mugs and serve it hot.
method_notes: All three steep a cinnamon stick in simmering water for about 5 minutes, blend old-fashioned oats with part of the milk, then cook the two together with sugar, stirring, until the drink coats a spoon, and finish with vanilla. In Mama Maggie's Kitchen uses plain milk and white sugar and cooks it for 15 minutes; Camila Made swaps in evaporated milk and brown sugar, and Maricruz Avalos uses twice the oats for a thicker atole and sprinkles cinnamon on top. This follows In Mama Maggie's Kitchen, scaled from 6 mugs to 4.
